CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing and chest pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Raymond is a patient presenting with difficulty swallowing that has persisted over several weeks. He reports pain with swallowing, particularly in the chest, that occurs with most foods but is most pronounced with larger pieces of food that feel stuck. He denies weight loss and notes he has actually gained approximately 10 pounds over the last month. Patient also reports occasional epigastric pain. He denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hematochezia, or melena. Patient is currently experiencing significant stress related to relocation from the west coast to the east coast. He reports recent dietary changes including increased consumption of pizza, burgers, alcohol, and caffeine due to the demands of the move.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, blood in stool, or dark tarry stool. Patient reports occasional epigastric pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented

MEDICATIONS
None documented

ALLERGIES
None documented

FAMILY HISTORY
None documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast and reports high stress related to the move and concerns about transporting his dog. He plans to drive for the relocation, which he anticipates will be a long trip. Current diet consists of pizza and burgers. He consumes alcohol and caffeine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 133/70 mmHg, heart rate normal, afebrile, O2 saturation 100% on room air, respiratory rate 19 breaths/min. Weight gain of 10 pounds documented over the last month. Head and Neck: No oral ulcers or thrush. Tonsils midline. No cervical adenopathy or thyromegaly. Abdomen: Nondistended with active bowel sounds. No pain to palpation of epigastric area. Negative Murphy's sign. No peritoneal signs or rebound. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Skin: No rash, lesions, or bruising. Eyes: Equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow: Two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Patient prescribed Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning and Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to reduce gastric acid production and coat the esophageal and gastric lining. Patient instructed to modify diet by decreasing alcohol and caffeine, avoiding citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve, eating slowly, and chewing food thoroughly. Upper endoscopy scheduled to rule out other pathology. Follow-up appointment in one week for endoscopy. Patient counseled on the importance of dietary modifications and healthy eating after relocation to facilitate recovery.
